_readme: Single source of truth for CI's `acceptance` matrix: the full fixture/filter/simulator/wave/shard definitions for every acceptance-family fixture. Both Scripts/ci-route.sh (to build the targeted, filtered matrix for a path-routed run) and .github/workflows/ci.yml's own 'full matrix' fallback (an unrouted run reads this same file in full, via the same script -- see ci-route.sh's `acceptance_matrix` output) read this one file, so there is exactly one place that knows the full fixture list rather than two independently-maintained copies that can silently drift apart. Per-fixture historical/rationale comments (why cli-commands is simulator "1" despite looking host-only, why xcode-wave-early-kill needs wave, why the four xcode-batch-testing-family fixtures exist at all, ...) are NOT duplicated here -- JSON has no comment syntax, and duplicating prose that can drift from the code it explains is worse than one clear pointer. See .github/workflows/ci.yml's own comment block directly above the `acceptance` job for that narrative, and Tests/MutantKitTests/Unit/CIAcceptanceMatrixClassificationTests.swift for the regression tests that keep this file, the real acceptance test suites, and ci.yml's wiring honest against each other.
_shard_readme: `shard`: one of "A"/"B"/"C"/"D", consulted only on a full-matrix run (Scripts/ci-route.sh groups every fixture by this field into 4 `acceptance` matrix jobs instead of 18 -- see that script's own header comment for why: GitHub Pro's hosted macOS runners cap concurrent jobs at 5, so 18 individual acceptance jobs queue in waves and each one separately re-pays SwiftPM-cache-restore + build-artifact-download/extract + simulator-boot overhead that a shard now pays once per 4-5 fixtures instead of once per fixture). Ignored on a targeted (path-routed) run -- there, ci-route.sh puts each selected fixture in its own single-fixture shard instead, which preserves today's per-fixture parallelism exactly (targeted runs already select only a handful of fixtures, so the 18-job scheduling problem this grouping solves does not apply there, and collapsing them would only add latency for no benefit). The 4 groups below were sized once, on 2026-08-23, from the real per-fixture wall-clock time (job start to job end, excluding queue wait) of every `acceptance` matrix entry in the full-matrix run of GitHub Actions run id 33256426157 (PR #22's merge to main, https://github.com/juntaki/mutantkit/actions/runs/33256426157), fed as weights into a Longest-Processing-Time-first greedy bin-pack across 4 bins -- see that run's own per-job timings for the exact seconds used. Result: shard A/B/C/D total roughly 1578-1594s (~26.3-26.6 min) each, i.e. close to evenly loaded, and (because 18 separate jobs' cache-restore/artifact-download/simulator-boot overhead collapses into 4) each shard's *actual* wall-clock after this change should come in under that sum, not above it. Re-tune later by pulling fresh per-job timings from a subsequent full-matrix run (`gh api repos/juntaki/mutantkit/actions/runs/<run-id>/jobs` gives per-job started_at/completed_at) and re-running the same LPT bin-pack -- there is no requirement to keep exactly these 4 groups forever, only to keep every fixture assigned to exactly one shard and the shards reasonably balanced.
